title: The email thread is real; the bank account is new
scenario: A supplier replies inside a months-old invoice thread and says future payments should go to a new bank account after a merger. The writing style and signatures match earlier messages.

answers.A: Trust the change because the attacker would need access to the real thread to reply inside it.
answers.B: Verify the bank change through a known supplier contact and approved vendor-master process outside the email thread.
answers.C: Ask the supplier to confirm the change in your procurement/vendor portal.

explanation: Business email compromise often uses genuine compromised mailboxes and real threads. Thread continuity is not payment authentication.
proTip: A real thread can carry a fraudulent destination.
